title: "Hope Is Not an Investment Strategy," Says the Lone Wall Street Analyst Who Hasn't Been Wrong About SpaceX
author: Sean Williams
description: SpaceX stock has fallen 15% below its IPO price and 50% from its all-time high, with 37 of 38 Wall Street analysts rating it a buy or hold. However, CFRA analyst Keith Snyder's sell rating and $115 price target have proven prescient. Snyder argues that SpaceX's $28.5 trillion addressable market claim is questionable, the company lacks recurring profits despite positive adjusted EBITDA, and Elon Musk's history of unfulfilled promises (Tesla's Level 5 autonomy, robotaxis) suggests investors shouldn't rely on hope when valuing the stock.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock trading 15% below IPO price and 50% off all-time high. Only analyst with sell rating has been correct. Company lacks recurring profits, is capital-intensive, prone to delays, and CEO has history of unfulfilled promises. Valuation not justified by fundamentals.

title: OPEC+ Is About to Pause Oil Output Hikes. Here's What It Means for Oil Stocks.
author: Matt Dilallo
description: OPEC+ is expected to pause production increases after September, maintaining current output levels through year-end. This pause could keep crude prices elevated as global markets rebuild stockpiles disrupted by Strait of Hormuz tensions. The decision may also prompt Iraq to leave OPEC, potentially benefiting U.S. oil companies with operations there like Chevron and ConocoPhillips.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Chevron has signed memorandums of understanding with Iraq covering two oil fields, including potential operational control of West Qurna 2. If Iraq leaves OPEC due to production quota constraints, Chevron could accelerate production growth and expand operations in the country.

ConocoPhillips recently agreed to acquire a 42% interest in BP Energy Company of Kirkuk with access to four large-scale oil fields holding 3 billion barrels. If Iraq leaves OPEC and increases production, ConocoPhillips could invest more and accelerate production growth.

BP is partnering with ConocoPhillips in Iraq's Kirkuk operations. If Iraq leaves OPEC and increases production quotas, BP could benefit from expanded development and optimization of the four oil fields.

title: This Industrial Stock Is Up 533% in 2 Years. I Predict It Will Join the Dow if Caterpillar Issues a Stock Split.
author: Daniel Foelber
description: GE Vernova has surged 533% in two years and could potentially join the Dow Jones Industrial Average if Caterpillar issues a stock split to rebalance the index's industrial sector weighting. The company supplies heavy-duty gas turbines for AI data centers and trades at a reasonable 30.8 P/E ratio, though earnings growth is expected to decelerate after 2026, making it suitable only for risk-tolerant investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 533% two-year performance and industry-leading position in AI data center equipment supply. However, sentiment is tempered by expected earnings deceleration after 2026 and cyclical risk exposure.

title: Brent Crude Tops $100 After Reports of Tanker Attacks Near Saudi Arabia. Should Investors Buy Oil Stocks Now?
author: Matt Dilallo
description: Brent crude surged 7% to over $100 a barrel following reports of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian oil tankers in the Red Sea. With ongoing disruptions to oil supply routes via the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, Goldman Sachs warns crude could reach $120 a barrel. Despite oil's 65% surge this year, major oil stocks have only gained modestly, presenting potential upside for investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Oil price surge to $100+ barrel benefits Chevron significantly. The company has delivered structural cost reductions and is positioned to generate higher earnings and cash flow at elevated crude prices. Stock has only gained 30% YTD despite 65% oil surge, suggesting upside potential.

title: SoFi Investors Just Got Great News From JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs
author: Jennifer Saibil
description: Strong earnings from major banks JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs, driven by robust investment banking and lending activity, signal a healthy economy that should benefit smaller banks like SoFi. With lending up significantly and the SpaceX IPO boosting retail investment platforms, SoFi is well-positioned ahead of its Q2 earnings report on July 29.
